_comment: THE LINEAGE SCREEN'S TRIGGER TABLE for 2002 (lineage_screen.py, kb/Work PB5589; DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md
section 10.5). A trigger FLAGS a candidate pair whose identical words are known to govern something else in 2002; an
unflagged pair is not thereby the same requirement, and every pair is decided by a read of the 2002 rule in the 2002
text. A change record for a flagged pair answers each flag by the trigger's name (next.answers), or it is refused.
`triggers`: each by mechanism (the only code), its parameters, the field or text it reads, and the reason its flag
gives; `measured-only: true` flags nothing and is scored against the labels. `pending`: the judgment of a changed or
removed 2002 pending clause (its counterpart where the title match is wrong, the 2002 clauses whose rules rest on it,
the words that invoke it, why); a changed clause with no judgment flags every pair under it and every pair naming its
title. `behaviours`: the 2002 clauses of each compiler dialect behaviour that differs between 2002 and 2023; one with
no entry flags every pair. `holds`: pairs held by evidence no text shows (the S1 run's refusals of a construct the

triggers.name: ambiguous
triggers.reason: the rule pairs with more than one 2023 rule

triggers.name: normalized
triggers.reason: the texts are the same only after typography is erased

triggers.name: absent-from-2014
triggers.reason: the rule's whole text is not in the 2014 text, so the identity of the words is not continuous across editions

triggers.name: definition-changed
triggers.reason: the rule uses a term whose 2023 definition differs from 2002's

triggers.name: definition-dropped
triggers.reason: the rule uses a term 2002 defines and 2023's definitions clause does not (its meaning rests on where 2023 now defines it)

triggers.name: cross-reference
triggers.reason: the rule refers to another clause by number, whose content may differ

triggers.name: pending-clause
triggers.reason: the rule depends on a pending clause whose text changed or is gone in 2023

triggers.name: behaviour-switch
triggers.reason: the rule's clause holds a behaviour the compiler switches between 2002 and 2023

triggers.name: held
triggers.reason: the rule is held by evidence no text shows

triggers.name: band-formats
triggers.reason: the formats the rule's band governs in 2002 are not those its counterpart's band governs

triggers.name: clause-identity
triggers.reason: the rule's clause is not the same set of rows in both editions (a row added, removed, unpaired or moved)
triggers.why-measured: it marks 83 of the first sample's 84 SAME pairs, so it is scored and flags nothing

triggers.name: communication-reach

params.context: the 2002 communication section (Annex A, the CD entry)
params.confined: \b(?:only|shall be specified only) in the (?:file|working-storage|local-storage|linkage|report|screen) section

triggers.source: §2002:A (the communication facility; §2002:G.2 item 1, obsolete) and the 2002 catalog's FMT-13.14 rows
triggers.reason: the rule governs entries a 2002 CD entry can hold (the communication section, §2002:A), a reach its words do not show

triggers.name: removed-element
triggers.source: §2002:G.2 items 1-3 (communication facility; debugging lines and DEBUGGING MODE; PADDING CHARACTER), §2002:G.1 item 4 (ON OVERFLOW of CALL)
triggers.reason: the rule names an element 2002 marks obsolete (§2002:G.2) or archaic (§2002:G.1), whose 2002 rules the rule rests on

triggers.name: deferral
triggers.reason: the rule defers to other rules, whose content it does not state

sum-size-error-raised-at-addition.why: the SUM clause, §2002:13.16.52, whose additions into a sum counter run during the GENERATE (§2002:14.8.15) and TERMINATE (§2002:14.8.42) statements and set only the size error indicator at 2002

integer-argument-rounded-under-standard-.why: the 31-digit rounding of a standard intermediate function argument, §2002:8.8.1.3.1.3 situation 2, from which §2002:15.34.3 RV1 exempts the INTEGER function's argument at 2002 alone (kb/Work PB5575, VCR row 7.81)

select-when-only-for-file-phrase-stateme.why: the SELECT WHEN clause, §2002:13.16.49, evaluated for every WRITE and REWRITE (§2002:14.8.33, §2002:14.8.47) of a FORMAT or CODE-SET file

compile-time-arithmetic-mode.why: compile-time arithmetic: the directives of §2002:7.2 and the constant entry §2002:13.9

compile-time-arithmetic-is-standard-deci.why: compile-time arithmetic: the directives of §2002:7.2 and the constant entry §2002:13.9

currency-picture-symbol-literal-alphanum.why: the CURRENCY SIGN clause of the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, §2002:12.2.6, whose literal-8 is an alphanumeric literal that no two occurrences may repeat at 2002 (§2002:12.2.6.2 SR22; kb/Work PB5707, VCR row 7.127)

currency-hexadecimal-literal-rules.why: the CURRENCY SIGN clause of the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, §2002:12.2.6, whose literal-7 and literal-8 rules (§2002:12.2.6.2 SR18, SR22) name no hexadecimal form at 2002 (kb/Work PB5595, PB6031, VCR row 7.116)

exception-statement-is-63-characters.why: the EXCEPTION-STATEMENT function, §2002:15.27, whose returned values RV1 and RV2 are 31 characters at 2002 (kb/Work PB5698, PB5717, VCR row 7.117)

flow-global-exit-is-never-set.why: the EXIT statement, §2002:14.8.13 (GR2 sets EC-FLOW-GLOBAL-EXIT for an EXIT within the range of a GLOBAL declarative), and the GOBACK statement, §2002:14.8.17 (GR3 and GR4 make a GOBACK in a function or method that EXIT), where §2023 states no rule that sets it (kb/Work PB5715, VCR row 7.118)

float-edited-picture-wide-bounds.why: the PICTURE clause, §2002:13.16.38, whose floating-point exponent (GR12) is three digits and whose digit positions (SR6) are 1 through 31 at 2002 (kb/Work PB5712, VCR row 7.119)

address-of-subordinate-strong-group-need.why: the data-address-identifier's syntax rules, §2002:8.4.2.11.2, whose SR4 requires a strongly-typed group item to be defined with its own TYPE clause referencing a STRONG declaration, a rule §2023:8.4.3.11.3 drops (kb/Work PB5705, VCR row 7.125)

prototype-special-names-admit-alphabet-a.why: the compilation group, §2002:10.5, whose SR5c limits a prototype's SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph to the LOCALE, CURRENCY and DECIMAL-POINT clauses at 2002 (kb/Work PB5706, VCR row 7.127)

parameter-name-appears-once-in-using-cla.why: the CLASS-ID paragraph, §2002:11.2, and the INTERFACE-ID paragraph, §2002:11.5, whose syntax rules carry no rule against a repeated parameter-name in the USING clause at 2002 (GR5 / GR3: the name given to the formal parameter), where §2014:11.3.2 SR9 and §2014:11.6.2 SR7 refuse one (kb/Work PB5753, VCR row 7.129)

turn-directive-repeats-only-name-file-co.why: the TURN directive's syntax rules, §2002:7.2.19.2, whose SR3 refuses an exception-name specified more than once in one TURN directive, where §2023:7.3.25.3 SR3 refuses only a repeated exception-name and file-name combination (kb/Work PB5725, VCR row 7.126)

constant-length-subscripts-are-literals.why: the constant entry, §2002:13.9, whose SR3 says only that data-name-1 and data-name-2 may be qualified, so a subscript of the LENGTH OF / BYTE-LENGTH OF operand is an ordinary one at 2002 (kb/Work PB5709, VCR row 7.121)

implied-dollar-currency-clause.why: the CURRENCY SIGN clause of the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, §2002:12.2.6, whose SR24 asks the class of a written literal-7 only and implies no '$' clause at 2002 (kb/Work PB5614, VCR row 7.120)

call-restricted-pointer-signature-same.why: the CALL statement, §2002:14.8.4, whose GR7 lets program-prototype-name-1 decide the called program's characteristics and asks no agreement with a restricted program-pointer's prototype at 2002 (kb/Work PB5714, VCR row 7.121)

call-any-length-operand-rule-by-format.why: the CALL statement, §2002:14.8.4, whose SR10 (ALL FORMATS) forbids an ANY LENGTH identifier-2, identifier-3 and identifier-4 in every format at 2002 (kb/Work PB5611, VCR row 7.122)

relative-read-previous-after-open-compar.why: the READ statement, §2002:14.8.29, whose GR18c2 compares 'less than or equal to' the file position indicator for PREVIOUS after an OPEN, where §2023 relative rule b) ignores the direction (kb/Work PB5742, VCR row 7.123)

move-sign-is-the-values-sign.why: the MOVE statement, §2002:14.8.24, whose GR4b1 places the sign of the sending operand at 2002 (kb/Work PB5852, VCR row 7.85); every statement that stores by the MOVE rules sends its store through it

line-sequential-file-rules.why: the RECORD DELIMITER clause, §2002:12.3.4.11, whose method frames a variable-length record; the READ statement, §2002:14.8.29, whose GR13 makes a record outside the minimum and maximum size a record length conflict; and the WRITE statement, §2002:14.8.47, which writes the record at its size: a file the line delimiter frames keeps those rules until 2023 (kb/Work PB5903, VCR row 7.88)
